newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Evergreen Marine to buy 30 more ships.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen Marine to buy 30 more ships.

text.p: Taiwan's shipping giant Evergreen Marine said on Wednesday it plans to buy another 30 container ships for future expansion and one local newspaper estimated the cost to be around US$1 billion.
"We do have a long-term plan to buy 30 more container ships around the year 2000, but the details have yet to be finalised," a company spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.

The local Economic Daily News said on Wednesday Evergreen Marine plans to buy 30 more container ships with loading capacity of each ship ranging between 1,500 and 2,500 twenty-foot-equivalent-unit (TEUs), which will cost some US$1 billion.
The spokeswoman declined to confirm the figures.
This followed an October 1996 Evergreen announcement that it had decided to buy another eight 5,364 TEUs container ships at an estimated cost of US$600 million.
Evergeen said last October it would buy eight ships from Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, but the spokeswoman on Wednesday declined to say from which company it planned to buy the 30 ships.
Evergreen now has 61 ships on order after Wednesday's announcement and once all the vessels are delivered, its fleet will increase to 146 from 85 ships now.
